problem_statement: The IPv6-to-IPv4 translation routine, ip64_6to4(), accepts malformed input and copies bytes beyond the bounds of the buffers it is given. A caller that hands it an IPv6 packet whose length field claims more payload bytes than were actually received gets a successful (non-zero) result, and the translation writes a copy that runs past the end of both the source packet and the destination buffer; a packet that is even shorter than an IPv6 header is likewise not refused. A caller can observe this without a sanitizer: when ip64_6to4() is invoked with such a malformed packet and a destination buffer surrounded by untouched sentinel bytes, those bytes past the capacity the caller supplied are clobbered. The required behavior is that ip64_6to4() rejects (returns 0 and produces no output copy) any packet whose length field exceeds the payload that was actually received, and any packet that is too short to hold an IPv6 header, leaving the destination buffer untouched.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: ip64_6to4() must validate the IPv6 length field against the bytes received after the header, refuse a packet shorter than an IPv6 header, and ensure the translated IPv4 packet fits BUFSIZE, instead of comparing the field against the whole received length (which let a field claiming one header more than the packet held pass and overran the destination buffer).
check_issues: `problem_statement` names code of the fix that the tests do not use (BUFSIZE); describe what a caller observes instead

causal_chain: The upstream test sixto4_rejects_bad_length invokes ip64_6to4() directly with a malformed packet: first with an IPv6 length field set to the full received length (overstating the payload by one header) and a destination buffer padded with sentinel bytes, asserting the call returns 0 and the sentinel region is unchanged; then with a packet shorter than an IPv6 header, again asserting a 0 return and an undisturbed buffer. Before the production fix the routine accepts these inputs and copies past the buffer, so both the return-value and the sentinel-intactness assertions fail; after the fix the inputs are rejected and the assertions pass. The test is registered and run in the native test-ip64 runner, so the case fails before and passes after the production change.

verification.reason: The problem statement already specifies the public function, the required rejection behavior for malformed length and too-short packets, the return value, and the no-output/untouched-buffer guarantee checked by the hidden test.
